title: Pentagon Bets $150M on Rare-Earth-Free Magnets as US Unleashes $3B Minerals Blitz, SpaceX-Nvidia Deal Reshapes AI Compute Landscape
subhead: The Trump administration announced the largest single-day federal capital deployment into critical minerals — $3 billion — including a $150M Pentagon bet on iron nitride magnets that could render China's rare earth leverage moot. Meanwhile, SpaceX's exclusive Nvidia partnership threatens to squeeze neocloud competitors, and data center moratoriums are spreading across the US.

sections.heading: Pentagon's $150M Iron Nitride Bet Targets China's Rare Earth Chokepoint
sections.body:
Buried inside the Trump administration's $3 billion critical minerals announcement on Friday was a $150 million conditional loan to Minneapolis-based Niron Magnetics — a startup whose technology doesn't diversify the rare earth supply chain. It eliminates the need for rare earths entirely.

Niron's magnets are made from iron nitride (α″-Fe₁₆N₂), using iron ore and atmospheric nitrogen. No neodymium, no dysprosium, no terbium, no Chinese processing facility required. The theoretical saturation magnetization reaches approximately 2.4 Tesla, exceeding the best grades of neodymium-iron-boron permanent magnets, according to TechTimes. The Pentagon's bet is that the technology solves the geopolitical problem for a critical subset of defense applications — actuators, guided munitions, robotics — that don't require the most extreme operating temperatures (the material decomposes above ~250°C).

Niron is already partnered with Moog Inc. for rare earth-free actuators in guided munitions systems and has $33 million in backing from GM Ventures and Stellantis Ventures. Its 287,000-square-foot facility in Sartell, Minnesota targets 1,500 metric tons of annual magnet production by early 2027, creating 175 jobs.

The broader $3 billion package includes a $1.4 billion conditional loan to Sila Nanotechnologies for silicon-carbon anode manufacturing at its Moses Lake, Washington plant, a $400 million loan to Australia's Sunrise Energy Metals for scandium mining (a mineral used in fighter aircraft), and $58 million in Export-Import Bank lending to Westwater Resources, Global Advanced Metals, and 5E Advanced Materials.

According to CNBC, Trump told more than 200 mining executives at the State Department: 'We're reclaiming America's rightful place as the minerals superpower of the world.' The Department of Energy also announced $100 million in grants for mining schools, with a goal of doubling mining-related graduates within two years, while the Pentagon committed $80 million for mining school projects. Officials pointed to China's network of mining universities as a key advantage the US needs to counter.

The urgency is driven by the Iran conflict, which has depleted US weapons stockpiles of precision-guided missiles and air-defense interceptors, per CNBC. Rare earths, tungsten, germanium, and scandium are essential for manufacturing those systems. Meanwhile, China's suspension of expanded rare earth export controls expires on November 10, 2026 — three months away. When it lapses, a broad licensing system covering medium and heavy rare earths, processing technology, and magnet manufacturing could be reimposed.
sections.whyItMatters: The iron nitride bet is the first major US attempt to make China's rare earth leverage structurally irrelevant rather than just building parallel supply chains. If Niron scales, it changes the calculus for a class of defense applications — but the technology is 3-7 years from full EV traction motor deployment, and the November 10 expiration of China's rare earth export suspension adds urgency.

sections.heading: Mecca Defence Pact Creates New Security Architecture, Turkey Says Egypt May Join
sections.body:
Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement on August 7, establishing a collective defense compact where an attack on one signatory is treated as an attack on all — language that Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan described as 'technically the same as NATO's Article 5,' according to Reuters.

The following day, Fidan said Egypt could join the agreement and that the pact 'will grow over time to bring all countries under this umbrella,' as reported by India TV. Fidan explicitly stated that 'Iran is not the target of this alliance,' but Iran's parliament member Ebrahim Rezaei responded by threatening that 'a paper agreement with Turkey and Pakistan does not bring Saudi Arabia security.'

For Turkey's defense-industrial sector, the pact opens a new channel. Saudi analyst Hesham Alghannam told AFP that if proxy attacks on Saudi territory escalate, 'Pakistan would deepen its air defence and advisory role inside the kingdom, and Turkey would accelerate defence-industrial transfers' — a reference to Turkey's growing drone and defense exports, anchored by Baykar's TB2 and Akıncı platforms.

The pact was signed after three years of discussions and formalized at Al-Safa Palace in Mecca. It comes amid the US-Iran conflict, with Saudi Arabia facing drone strikes from Iran-backed Iraqi militias and Houthis targeting its oil infrastructure.
sections.whyItMatters: The Mecca pact is the first formal NATO-Article-5-equivalent security structure in the Gulf, and Turkey's inclusion as a defense-industrial supplier gives it a new export channel for its drone and weapons systems. If Egypt joins, the bloc would span the eastern Mediterranean to the Indian Ocean, creating an alternative security architecture that doesn't depend on the US.

sections.heading: SpaceX-Nvidia Exclusive Deal Threatens Neocloud Competitors
sections.body:
SpaceX's aggressive push into AI compute is reshaping the GPU allocation landscape. The company is exclusively using Nvidia's technology and will receive a 'very significant percent' of Nvidia's 2027 GPU supply, CEO Elon Musk said, according to MarketWatch. SpaceX has already signed compute deals with Anthropic ($1.25 billion/month), Alphabet, and Reflection AI, with another major deal starting in October that analysts hypothesize could be the US Defense Department or Microsoft.

Bernstein analysts warned that 'Nvidia will bump SpaceX to the front of the line for GPU capacity, even ahead of the neoclouds it has stood up,' threatening companies like CoreWeave and Nebius that depend on GPU supply access. SpaceX says AI compute demand could help it reach a $100 billion annualized revenue run rate by year-end.

The squeeze comes as neoclouds already face mounting pressure. CoreWeave's debt is expected to grow to $33 billion from $25 billion in Q1, and both it and Nebius report steeper per-share losses year-over-year despite revenue growth. BNP Paribas analyst Stefan Slowinski noted SpaceX is being 'much more aggressive' than Meta in compute provisioning.
sections.whyItMatters: SpaceX's privileged GPU access threatens to create a new bottleneck for AI infrastructure. If Nvidia prioritizes SpaceX — its exclusive partner — over neocloud providers, smaller compute brokers face an existential supply problem, concentrating AI compute further into fewer hands.

sections.heading: Data Center Moratoriums Spread as Trump Battles Local Pushback
sections.body:
A growing wave of local pushback against data center construction is colliding with federal AI policy. Texas Governor Greg Abbott imposed a moratorium on data center grid interconnections this week, and Bloomberg NEF estimates this puts ~20% of the total US data center pipeline at risk of delay, according to Seeking Alpha.

President Trump publicly rebuked the move, calling it a 'mistake' and saying AI data centers 'could be bigger than oil,' per multiple reports. New York Governor Kathy Hochul had already enacted a first-in-the-nation statewide moratorium on large-scale data centers on July 14, and communities from Massachusetts to Florida are following suit with their own restrictions, according to the Boston Herald.

The conflict is playing out at the intersection of energy policy and national AI competitiveness. Data centers are projected to fuel almost half the growth in US electricity demand by 2030, and local officials cite power grid strain and water consumption as primary concerns. Yakima County in Washington state is considering its own moratorium, and Pinellas Park, Florida has paused data center permits.
sections.whyItMatters: The data center moratorium trend directly threatens the infrastructure buildout needed for US AI supremacy. Texas alone represents ~20% of the national pipeline — if more states follow New York's lead, the physical backbone of the AI economy gets harder to build on American soil.

sections.heading: Space Debris Economy Takes Shape as SpaceX Rocket Crashes Into Moon
sections.body:
A spent SpaceX Falcon 9 upper stage crashed into the moon this week, more than a year after being left on an uncontrolled trajectory following a lunar mission. The incident highlighted the growing problem of orbital debris just as companies are positioning to turn cleanup into a business.

According to OrbitRadar, there are nearly 30,000 tracked objects in space, of which only about 18,500 are active satellites. The ESA's Tim Flohrer warned that debris is fragmenting faster than it naturally re-enters the atmosphere, potentially making 'certain orbits unusable.'

Tokyo-listed Astroscale reported a 142% revenue surge in its most recent fiscal year and has demonstrated orbital docking via magnetic capture systems. Its commercial VP Andrew Faiola told CNBC that 'space is a global commons, and we're mucking it up.' Luxembourg-based ClearSpace is developing a broader in-orbit servicing model — inspection, repair, and maintenance — comparing it to the road and aviation maintenance industries.

Both companies still rely heavily on government contracts and are burning cash. But the defense sector is growing as a customer, with Astroscale noting growing demand for applications with military relevance.
sections.whyItMatters: The space debris problem is shifting from a scientific concern to a commercial and military opportunity. With 30,000+ tracked objects and constellations multiplying, the companies that solve orbital cleanup are positioning themselves at the intersection of commercial space and national security.

sections.heading: Water Utility Cyberattacks: Mojtabas Army Emerges as Suspected Actor
sections.body:
The wave of cyberattacks targeting water systems across 12 US states — including Michigan, Minnesota, Georgia, New Jersey, and South Dakota — has been attributed to a group calling itself 'Mojtabas Army,' according to multiple reports. The group is testing a new form of cyber warfare that could have turned water supplies toxic, raising questions about whether US critical infrastructure has adequate visibility into its own exposed systems.

Cape May, New Jersey mayor Zack Mullock called the hack 'modern warfare' after his town's water system was breached. Texarkana Water Utilities confirmed they are taking steps to secure local infrastructure. The attacks follow a pattern identified by Forescout last year showing that many water utilities don't know what operational technology systems are exposed to the internet.

These attacks represent an escalation in infrastructure targeting that sits alongside the broader US-Iran conflict. While attribution remains ongoing, the timing and pattern of infrastructure probing is consistent with state-affiliated groups operating during active geopolitical confrontations.
sections.whyItMatters: The 12-state water utility attack demonstrates that critical infrastructure targeting has moved from espionage to operational disruption. The core vulnerability isn't just the attack — it's that many utilities don't know what's exposed on their networks. Without asset visibility, defense remains reactive.

sections.heading: Türkiye Tech Watch: Mecca Pact Opens Defense Export Channel
sections.body:
For Turkey's defense-industrial sector, the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement signed this week creates a formalized export pathway. Baykar's drone portfolio — the TB2 and Akıncı platforms that have already seen combat in Ukraine, Libya, and Ethiopia — stands to benefit from 'accelerated defence-industrial transfers' to Saudi Arabia, as analyst Hesham Alghannam described to AFP.

Turkey's defense exports have grown significantly in recent years, and the Mecca pact adds a collective-security framework that could institutionalize procurement channels between the three signatories. Foreign Minister Fidan's suggestion that Egypt could join the agreement would further expand the market for Turkish defense products.

However, the pact's actual operational meaning remains ambiguous. Fidan's insistence that Iran is not the target doesn't fully align with Saudi Arabia's immediate security concerns about Iranian-backed militias and Houthi drone strikes. Whether Turkey commits air defense systems to Saudi territory — or merely sells them — will be the telling signal.
sections.whyItMatters: Turkey's defense industry has been looking for institutionalized export relationships beyond ad hoc deals. The Mecca pact could provide that — but whether it functions as a mutual defense commitment or a defense procurement club depends on how Turkey and Pakistan respond to actual threats against Saudi territory.

bottomLine: The Trump administration's $3 billion minerals push is the largest single-day federal capital deployment into the sector on record, but the most consequential piece is a $150M bet on iron nitride — a material that could make China's rare earth leverage structurally irrelevant for defense applications. Combined with SpaceX's exclusive Nvidia GPU grab threatening neoclouds, and spreading data center moratoriums putting 20% of the US pipeline at risk, today's brief is about who controls the physical inputs of the next economy: rare earths, compute, and power. The Mecca defense pact adds a new layer, giving Turkey's defense exporters a formal channel into Gulf security architecture. And the 12-state water utility hack shows that infrastructure vulnerability remains the soft underbelly of all this hardware ambition.
sources: CNBC, TechTimes, MarketWatch/Morningstar, Seeking Alpha, Bloomberg NEF, Boston Herald, Reuters, India TV, AFP, CNBC Space, Defense Daily, Financial Express, MSN, NewsNation, Texarkana Gazette, Astroscale, Niron Magnetics, Sila Nanotechnologies
